Vai al grafo

Marionette

0.5.0

Clicca un nodo per i dettagli.

Come funziona il coordinatore

L’IA interpreta la richiesta e il contesto, confronta intenti ed esclusioni e seleziona le capability. Non usa parole chiave per scegliere una skill.

Le linee grigie collegano l’IA alle capability senza prerequisiti dichiarati: sono scelte disponibili, non passi da eseguire tutti. Le frecce blu indicano solo i prerequisiti after, validi sempre. Le frecce arancioni tratteggiate sono prerequisiti condizionati (needs): l’etichetta la riassume in poche parole; la condizione completa si legge cliccando la freccia o il nodo di arrivo, e la valuta l’IA per ogni richiesta; se vale, la capability di partenza entra nel piano prima dell’altra. Il flusso dei dati (reads) non è mostrato nella vista base, perché dipende dal lavoro scelto. Scegliendo un percorso compaiono frecce verdi piene dove chi produce viene prima di chi legge: lì i dati passano davvero. Scegliendo un intento compaiono frecce verdi tratteggiate: output che le capability di quell’intento possono usare o fornire, se l’altra capability è nel piano.

Una capability lavora alla volta. Un solo responsabile per output; conflitti e varianti incompatibili vengono rifiutati. Un prerequisito si salta solo se tutti i suoi output sono già registrati.

Esiti della decisione IA

selected: esegue il percorso validato. Un passo è diretto; più passi richiedono conferma se non già autorizzati.

needs_clarification: pone la domanda necessaria e si ferma. no_match: segnala che il catalogo non copre il risultato e si ferma.

classification-required: l’host deve produrre una decisione IA. Nessuna capability viene eseguita.

Comandi
/marionette
python muro.py plan --compact --task "<richiesta>" --project "<progetto>"
python muro.py plan --task "<richiesta>" --project "<progetto>" --classification "<cartella di stato>/classification.json" --confirm
python muro.py resume --project "<progetto>"

Ogni comando sta su una riga; i JSON li scrive l’host in un file della cartella di stato. Per i passi con mappa, invia output e verifiche in modo atomico con gli identificatori restituiti con il passo:

python muro.py step --project "<progetto>" --map-id <map_id> --capability <capability> --step-data "<cartella di stato>/step.json"
python muro.py complete --project "<progetto>" --map-id <map_id>

Per sostituire una mappa: nuova classificazione e plan --new. Il browser non esegue comandi.

Strumenti, attivatori e precedenze

I vincoli stack:* indicano compatibilità tecnica, non attivatori testuali. L’host verifica strumenti e autorizzazioni. Gli hook sono descrizioni passive, non vengono installati o attivati automaticamente.

Catalogo completo

Work Map Coordinatorwork-map

Responsabilità: coordinator

Intenti e attivazione

L’IA valuta il risultato desiderato e il contesto. Questi intenti non sono parole chiave di attivazione.

engineering.work-coordination

Implement clear software changes directly; otherwise agree scope, resolve decisions, write a spec and build reviewed vertical slices with evidence.

Esclusioni e limiti

  • Not a fallback for unknown, ambiguous or non-engineering requests.
  • Do not add planning ceremony to a task that fits one direct step.
  • Designing a page, a design tool's file (Figma, FigCraft), motion, Office files or an explainer is the work of those capabilities, not engineering coordination.

Vincoli tecnici

Nessun vincolo di stack dichiarato. L’attivazione richiede comunque una selezione esplicita dell’IA.

Precedenze e collaborazioni

Prerequisiti dichiarati (after)

Nessun prerequisito dichiarato: può essere selezionata direttamente.

Capability che dichiarano questo prerequisito

Nessuna. Il completamento non attiva automaticamente altri passaggi.

Prerequisiti condizionati (needs): li valuta l’IA caso per caso

Nessuno dichiarato.

Le frecce indicano precedenze, non attivazioni automatiche. Un passaggio già completato si salta solo quando tutti i suoi output sono registrati nella mappa corrente.

Altre capability dello stesso ruolo: selezione esclusiva

Nessun’altra capability con lo stesso ruolo.

Conflitti esplicitamente dichiarati

Nessun conflitto dichiarato; non è una garanzia di compatibilità semantica.

Output e passaggio del lavoro

  • task_map
  • spec
  • step_sequence

Output di altre capability che usa, se già registrati (reads)

Nessuno dichiarato: lavora dalla richiesta e dal progetto.

Ogni output ha un solo responsabile nel piano. Il passaggio ai successori è esplicito; le istruzioni complete riportano come consegnarlo.

Strumenti richiesti

file-access (richiesto)
Read the repository, its glossary and ADRs, implement authorized source and test changes, and write local spec and ticket files.

shell (opzionale)
Run the project's tests and checks for each built slice.

subagent (opzionale)
Run a research item as a background agent with a fresh context, as the source's research skill asks.

Hook e attivatori operativi

Nessun hook adottato nel catalogo. Non descrive eventuali file upstream non ispezionati.

Un hook con politica active è registrato dalla release sugli host elencati in Fonti della release. Ogni altro hook è una descrizione passiva: l’host verifica strumenti, permessi e condizioni. La guida non installa né esegue nulla.

# Work Map Coordinator

Coordinates an engineering change with the wayfinder method: agree the destination, resolve the open decisions, write one spec, slice it into vertical tickets, then build and review slice by slice. Everything stays local: no issue tracker, branch push or pull request.

The packaged originals are the full version: where this body differs, the original wins, except for the changes listed in the Sources section. Open only the section a step names, when the task reaches it.

## Behavior

1. **Size the route first.** A map needs both: the effort is larger than one agent session can hold, and the route to the destination is unclear. Judge by session count, not project size; legacy and half-built codebases qualify as much as greenfield.
   - A well-scoped change that can be settled in one sitting: no map. Reuse the user's authorization and build directly (step 6) with check evidence; ask how to proceed only if the requested action is still unresolved.
   - The deciding is already done: skip the map and write the spec (step 4).
   - Many sessions and the route still unclear: chart the map (steps 2 and 3).
   - Unsure where the task sits: open `<package_root>/scripts/wayfinder/docs/engineering/wayfinder.md`, `## When to reach for it` and `## Common questions`.
2. **Name the destination** with the user: the spec, decision or change the whole map (not this session) is finding its way to. It fixes the scope, so it is agreed before any decision item exists.
3. **Chart and resolve decisions.** The map plans and does not build: every item is a question whose answer is a decision.
   - Map the frontier breadth-first: fan out over the whole space for the open decisions and the steps takeable now. If that surfaces no fog (the way is clear and the journey fits one session), no map is needed: return to step 1.
   - `task_map` is the map body: Destination, Notes, Decisions so far, Not yet specified, Out of scope. Open `<package_root>/scripts/wayfinder/skills/engineering/wayfinder/SKILL.source.md`, `### The map body`, when you write it. The map is an index, not a store: a decision is recorded in one place and the map only gists it and points there. Refer to items by title, never by a bare number.
   - Each open item is one question sized to one 100K token agent session. It is typed research (AFK), prototype (HITL), grilling (HITL, the default) or task (HITL or AFK), and may declare the items that block it. Open `## Ticket Types` of the same file when the type is not obvious.
   - Fog or item: the test is whether the question can be stated precisely now, not whether it can be answered now. A sharp question is an item even when blocked; the rest stays, unsliced, in Not yet specified (`## Fog of war`).
   - Never resolve more than one item per session, research items excepted. A HITL item resolves only through the live exchange with the user; the agent never answers for the human.
   - A `task` item does manual work that unblocks a decision; it never delivers part of the destination. One that looks like a slice of the build is mis-typed. Read the Notes of any map you did not chart, and keep implementation in separate sessions.
   - After each answer: record it with its item and close the item, add one line to Decisions so far, add newly surfaced items, and move fog that became specifiable out of Not yet specified into items. Work found to sit beyond the destination is closed with one line (gist and why) under Out of scope, not under Decisions so far; it never graduates (`## Out of scope`). If the decision invalidates other parts of the map, update or delete those items.
   - Charting is one session's work and hand-resolves nothing. When the map looks off, open the guide's `## It's working if`.
4. **Write the spec** once nothing is left to decide. Do not interview the user: synthesize what is already known. Explore the repository if not yet done, use its domain glossary vocabulary and respect its ADRs. Sketch the test seams: prefer existing seams to new ones, use the highest seam possible, propose any new one at the highest point; the fewer the better, ideally one. Check the seams with the user. Then open `<package_root>/scripts/wayfinder/skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.source.md`, `<spec-template>`, and fill every section: Problem Statement, Solution, User Stories, Implementation Decisions, Testing Decisions, Out of Scope, Further Notes. No specific file paths or code snippets, except a decision-rich snippet from a prototype, trimmed and marked as such.
5. **Slice it** into tracer-bullet tickets (`<package_root>/scripts/wayfinder/skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.source.md`, `## Process`).
   - Work from the context already present; read a referenced spec in full. Use the glossary vocabulary, respect ADRs, and look for prefactoring that makes the change easy.
   - Each slice is a narrow but complete path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests), never a horizontal slice of one layer; demoable or verifiable on its own; sized for a single fresh context window; prefactoring first. Each declares its blocking edges.
   - A wide refactor (one mechanical change that breaks call sites everywhere) is the exception: sequence it expand–contract. Open `### 3. Draft vertical slices` for the batching and integration-branch rules when one appears.
   - Quiz the user: a numbered list with Title, Blocked by and What it delivers; ask whether the granularity is right, whether each blocking edge is genuine, and whether any ticket should be merged or split. Iterate until the user approves.
   - Write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first), with that file's `<local-ticket-template>`; never a single combined file. Tickets also avoid file paths and code snippets, with the same prototype exception.
6. **Build and review** (Muro extension). Build direct work when authorized. For sliced work take the frontier, any ticket whose blockers are all done, one slice at a time, in a session separate from planning.
   - Code follows `<package_root>/scripts/ponytail/SKILL.source.md`: `## Before you write` for scope, then `## The smallest complete change` (its six-step ladder, its rules and its "Never cut:" line). Open it when writing code if the permanent policy is not already in context.
   - The approved spec, the agreed test seams, the slices, another capability's design authority and a required engine stay authoritative; the ladder chooses only among the options they leave open.
   - Its `## Levels` (lite, full, ultra) apply when the user states that preference for the task; otherwise full, the default.
   - Run the required project checks at the agreed seam and verify each acceptance criterion.
   - Record actual checks, unchecked work and material risks, then review against the spec before the next slice. A separately requested report can use engineering-review; it is not a prerequisite.

## Output handoff

Return `task_map` (the route chosen and, for a charted map, its index), `spec` (the spec text or its local path, or why the route needed none) and `step_sequence` (the approved slices with blocking edges, acceptance criteria and per-slice evidence) as JSON strings. For a mapped step, submit them through the coordinator's `record` command with the step's `map_id` and `capability`. The wayfinder map is this capability's own output, not the coordinator's run map: do not edit `<state_dir>/map.md` or `<state_dir>/state.json`; the coordinator is their only writer.

## Specifics

- Muro's plan confirmation authorizes running this step; it does not replace the user's decisions inside it (destination, test seams, slice breakdown, HITL items). Reuse decisions and authorization already given; ask only for an unresolved choice.
- A research item follows the source's `research` skill (`<package_root>/scripts/wayfinder/skills/engineering/research/SKILL.source.md`): a background agent with a fresh context, primary sources and not a secondary write-up of them, one Markdown file that cites each claim's source, saved where the repository already keeps such notes. A host without subagents does the same work in the session.
- Do the work the source gives to its grilling, domain-modeling, prototype and implement skills inline: those skills are not selected (Sources).
- The source does not recommend local markdown, because material stored in the repo tends to persist by accident: tell the user which `.scratch/` files were written.
- The method has no fixed runtime dependency; assess and install what the authorized implementation needs under the package's runtime rule, preserving any required engine.

## Checks

- **route_sized_by_sessions**: the route (direct, spec only, or map) follows the session count and the presence of fog; a direct route reused authorization and asked only if the requested action was unresolved.
- **destination_scope_agreed**: the destination was agreed with the user before any decision item existed, and work ruled beyond it is listed under Out of scope.
- **decisions_resolved_by_owner**: every open item reads as a question; HITL items carry the user's own answer; nothing is left in Not yet specified before the spec.
- **spec_template_complete**: every template section is present, test seams were confirmed with the user, and the spec has no file paths or code snippets beyond the template's prototype exception.
- **slices_vertical_gated**: every slice is end to end and verifiable alone, has acceptance criteria and acyclic blocking edges, and the user approved the breakdown.
- **slice_evidence_recorded**: each built slice has actual test or check output against its acceptance criteria, affected callers and preserved safeguards; unchecked work and material risk are explicit, and an unbuilt slice stays open.

## Sources

- AI intent mapping: wayfinder, to-spec and to-tickets → engineering.work-coordination, from the wayfinder SKILL.md (map, tickets, charting, working the map), the wayfinder guide (trigger, FAQ, "It's working if"), the to-spec process and template and the to-tickets slicing, quiz and local-ticket sections.
- Source: wayfinder (mattpocock/skills@d1478fcb, release v1.3.2) — `skills/engineering/wayfinder/SKILL.md`, `docs/engineering/wayfinder.md`, `skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md`, `skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md` and, since 2026-11-17, `skills/engineering/research/SKILL.md` (the skill wayfinder gives its research items to; ADR-0026), packaged under `<package_root>/scripts/wayfinder/` (each `SKILL.md` as `SKILL.source.md`).
- Muro extension: step 6 (build and review) comes from this source's intake goal ("extend it through build and review without remote trackers"); the source itself plans and hands off.
- Source: ponytail (DietrichGebert/ponytail@7801d061243d7b753bad0e0b3c057cd250b11755, release v5.3.3, MIT) - `skills/ponytail/SKILL.md`, packaged as `<package_root>/scripts/ponytail/SKILL.source.md`. Its `## Before you write` and `## The smallest complete change` are also carried, in the same words, in the package's permanent policy.
- AI harmonization (2026-11-12): Ponytail enriches the existing implementation owner without another writer, output or prerequisite. Wayfinder keeps destination/spec/slices and meaningful user gates. A requested engineering-review report remains independent of per-slice acceptance review. Second pass the same day: the body is an entry prompt in the package's words with pointers to the sections a step needs.
- Changes for coexistence (ADR-0017):
  - The issue tracker is replaced by local records: none is provided here, the source then defaults to local markdown, and the intake goal says "without remote trackers". The map is the `task_map` output handed over through the coordinator; `wayfinder:` labels, child issues, claiming by assignee, native blocking links, resolution comments and a map given as URL or number have nothing to run on. An item states its type in words and its answer is recorded with it.
  - "tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`" is not followed: that setup skill is not selected.
  - Research findings are not put on a pushed `research/<name>` branch: the intake goal keeps the work local, so they stay local with a pointer from the item.
  - to-spec's publishing to the tracker with the `ready-for-agent` label and to-tickets' real-tracker form are not applied (same collision); the "Local files" form is followed as written.
  - "Call the Skill tool" for grilling, domain-modeling and prototype, and the guide's hand-offs to other skills of the source, are done inline: those skills are not selected and routing between a source's own skills competes with the coordinator. The `research` skill is selected: this step starts its background agent itself, not through the Skill tool, and a host without subagents does the research in the session (a step that host cannot run).
  - Open intake question (2026-11-17): the grilling, domain-modeling, prototype and implement skills of the same repository are named by wayfinder only by skill name, were never read, and stay unselected. Whether the package absorbs them is a decision on this source's selection.
  - `disable-model-invocation: true` and every slash form are not carried: the coordinator classifies by meaning.
  - "Stop and ask the user how they'd like to proceed" (no fog) is asked only when the request has not already answered it: the confirmed plan and a request for the change itself say how to proceed.
  - The source "hands off and does not continue into code"; step 6 continues to the build, by the intake goal, always in a step separate from the map.
  - Ponytail's phrase and slash activation, its session mode and `/ponytail lite|full|ultra` are not applied: activation competes with the coordinator and the package keeps no mode state. The rules are active through the permanent policy for code work; a level is a preference stated for the task.
  - Ponytail's closing lines ("what you skipped or did not check, and any risk") follow the permanent policy's ordering with i-have-adhd's one next action, because both sources claim the end of the reply.
  - Ponytail's ladder does not override an approved spec, a design authority or an engine another capability requires: it would bend that capability's work.
- Gap: the source's local-markdown tracker layout lives in `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`, which is not selected; only the to-tickets local file layout is used.
- Hooks: the selected Wayfinder files define none; its `skills/**/scripts/**` and `skills/**/agents/**` are excluded and uninspected. Ponytail's original lifecycle/state/UI hooks were inspected and explicitly excluded from the curated integration; none is adopted here.
- Harmonized by: prompts/harmonizer.md (2026-11-10 re-harmonization) — the earlier body described Muro runtime internals and checked Muro's own map; it is replaced by the source's method and checks of the engineering work. `spec` is added as an output because the source's spec is a distinct handoff between decisions and slices.
Visual Direction (landing page and website)visual-direction

Responsabilità: art-direction

Intenti e attivazione

L’IA valuta il risultato desiderato e il contesto. Questi intenti non sono parole chiave di attivazione.

ui.visual-direction

Design and build, or restyle, a landing page, marketing site or company website page with one fixed visual system (one approved typeface in named text styles on a fixed type scale, spacing and radius tokens, flat backgrounds, the hero, icons, motion, states and ship requirements), in the project's own stack; or stop at the recorded direction when only that is asked.

Esclusioni e limiti

  • A motion request does not by itself require redesign.
  • A static hero does not imply animation.
  • An app screen, dashboard, settings view or component library is interface work for design guidance, aesthetic direction and the prototype step, not a website page.
  • Slide decks (PowerPoint or HTML), Office files, a design tool's files (Figma, FigCraft) and interactive explainer articles have their own style steps.

Verifiche di un passo con questo intento:

  • single_primary_action
  • proof_supported
  • palette_applied
  • typography_consistent
  • visual_system_met
  • states_and_ship_met
  • mobile_checked

ui.landing-strategy

Define a landing page's offer, audience, one primary action, risk reversal, proof beside each claim, objections and a conversion-oriented outline and copy, alone or before the page is built.

Esclusioni e limiti

  • App screens do not require a sales funnel.
  • Copy for an email, an ad or a social post is not a landing page.

# Visual Direction (landing page and website)

Plans, writes, builds and checks a landing page, a marketing site or a company website page the way the pinned landing-page-design does: its Part A decides what the page says and how it is structured, its Part B is the visual system every visual value resolves through, and the page is built section by section. `<LP>` below stands for `<package_root>/scripts/ai-design-skills/skills/landing-page-design`.

## Behavior

`<LP>/SKILL.source.md` is the full version of this method. Open the section a step names when the task reaches it. Where this body and the original differ, the original wins, except for the changes listed under Sources.

0. **Scope by the selected intent.** Landing strategy alone stops after step 3 and opens only Part A, "B8. Content realism" and "Output format". A direction without a build stops after step 4. Record every output not produced as `not requested: <reason>`.
1. **Read what exists.** The project's stack and the pages it already has, the brief's material (logo, screens, photographs, prices, proof) and a project `DESIGN.md` (see Specifics). "A landing page is not a homepage": a landing page wins one intent, one offer, one audience, one primary action; a company website page that serves several intents keeps the visual system of step 4 and takes from Part A what its content needs.
2. **Intake** ("A1. Intake"). Gather purpose, audience and context, proof and assets, and constraints before designing or writing. Ask only for what is missing, and ask in one batch rather than one question at a time. If the user cannot answer, make a reasonable assumption, state it in one line, and continue. Do not stall the build.
3. **Strategy and copy, before any code.** Return, in order, the seven parts of "Output format" with the counts it gives: page outline, hero copy, benefits, how it works, FAQ, SEO/AEO (index or noindex by "A7. SEO and AEO") and the layout recommendation (one of A to D by "A3. Layout selection", and why). The outline follows "A2. Page structure", the mandatory tagline reveal section of B11 included. From "A4. Conversion rules": one primary CTA, never competing CTAs above the fold; at least one risk reducer (free trial, free plan, no credit card, cancel anytime, money back guarantee); move the FAQ earlier for high friction offers. Put proof directly beside the claim it supports. The final CTA is identical to the top one. Open A4, A5 and A8 for the remaining conversion rules, the copy formulas and the pitfalls; the copy rules of B1 apply (no hyphens inside text, no orphaned words). From "B8. Content realism": on a real product's page prices, guarantees, statistics, customer counts, testimonials and logos come from the user or a real source, and a missing fact is a clearly marked placeholder such as `{{price}}` or `{{testimonial}}`; invented people, brands and sample numbers belong to fictional demos and prototypes only.
4. **Fix the visual system** ("PART B — Visual system": every visual value must resolve through these rules instead of being invented ad hoc). Open B1 to B7 before any code and write on the plan what the page uses:
   - **Typeface** (B1): one of Geist, Manrope, Geist Mono, Poppins; never Inter, Roboto, Arial, Open Sans, Helvetica; one typeface per site, a pair only when the prompt explicitly asks for it (Geist Mono beside the main font only for code, data or numeric UI); never italic, never 900 / black.
   - **Text styles and scale** (B1): every piece of text uses one of the named styles (Heading, Title, Body, Button, Caption), every size lands on Tailwind's default type scale, an off-scale size snaps to the closest step below with its paired line height. Define each style once as a class or token in kebab case.
   - **Spacing and radius** (B2, B3): only the thirteen spacing values of the table; Tailwind's radius values, with the nested radius formula where the gap is under 32px.
   - **Colour and backgrounds** (B4, B5): flat backgrounds, never a gradient; in dark mode only the six listed background colours; never a border on only one side of a card; the hero heading's left to right text gradient is the one gradient.
   - **Icons** (B6): Phosphor, Solar or Iconamoon; never Material Icons or Material Symbols.
   - **Motion** (B7): the base curve and its durations, only `transform` and `opacity`, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected; the navigation and the scroll reveals as B7 describes them.
5. **Build section by section** in the order of "A6. Build order": hero, benefits, how it works, proof, FAQ, final CTA. Never rebuild the whole page on each iteration. The hero follows "B5. Hero section" (heading and subheading capped at 680px, line breaks where the thought breaks). The tagline reveal section follows "B11. Tagline reveal section (mandatory)": at least two lines, its own moment further down the page, words activating one at a time. Write real copy and system messages by B8, and give every interactive element the full state set of "B9. States": hover, active, focus, loading, empty, error; no dead links.
6. **Ship check.** Go through "B10. Ship requirements" item by item, the check at 390px wide included (no horizontal overflow, buttons keep their text inside, the primary action visible in the first screen), then the three blocks of "Quick checklist" line by line. Fix what fails.
7. **Report and record.** Report what was built, every assumption of step 2 with its one line, every placeholder left for a missing fact, every deviation from a rule with the instruction that asked for it, and what could not be checked. Then record for the handoff below:
   - `offer`, `page_outline`: the strategy and the outline of step 3 (for a page that is not a landing page, its main action and its sections).
   - `palette`: the theme, the background and text colours, the accent and where each came from (the user, the brand's material, a stated assumption).
   - `typography`: the typeface and the named text styles in use.
   - `layout`: the layout type of A3 and the sections in their order.
   - `constraints`: the rules later steps must keep, including the motion rules of B7 as applied, and any deviation from the source with its reason.
   - `page`: the files written, or `not requested`.

## Output handoff

Resolve `<package_root>` with the `package_root` returned beside these instructions, never against the consumer project. Return every required output key as a JSON string. For a mapped step, submit them through the coordinator's `record` command with the step's `map_id` and `capability`. Do not edit `<state_dir>/map.md` or `<state_dir>/state.json`; the coordinator is their only writer.

## Specifics

- **The user's explicit prompt wins** over a rule of the source ("Scope": "When the user's explicit prompt conflicts with a rule, the user wins"): follow it and record the deviation and its reason in `constraints`. A framework default never does ("When a rule here conflicts with a framework default, this file wins").
- **A project design file is such an instruction.** A `DESIGN.md` of the project that is not a starter or a reference (the recorded `design_file`, or the file found in the project) counts as the user's explicit instruction for the values it confirms: its confirmed colour tokens, typefaces, spacing, radius and component values are followed where a rule of the source says otherwise. Each deviation is recorded in `constraints`. Its `unresolved` entries and `proposed` values are not instructions, and where the file is silent the method decides. This step never rewrites `DESIGN.md`: a value the page needs and the file lacks is asked of the user, and the change belongs to `design-file` in its own step. A request in the turn that contradicts the file is followed and said to do so. Where the project runs design code checks (`design-check.config.json`), source code in the checked paths with a colour value, a colour function such as `rgb()` or `oklch()`, a utility palette class, a font family or a `must-avoid` effect the file does not permit fails them: use the project's tokens there, or say that the check will fail.
- **One owner of the look and of the page.** This step owns palette, typography and layout for the page it builds. Later steps consume these outputs and do not restyle independently. Recorded `design_candidates` of `design-guidance` are candidates: Part B decides typeface, scale, spacing and backgrounds.

## Checks

- **single_primary_action**: one offer, one audience and one primary action are explicit, with no competing CTA above the fold; the final CTA is identical to the top one.
- **proof_supported**: on a real product's page every price, guarantee, statistic, customer count, testimonial and logo comes from the user or a real source, or is a clearly marked placeholder; proof sits beside the claim it supports. Invented names, brands and sample numbers appear only in a fictional demo or prototype.
- **palette_applied**: backgrounds are flat, dark mode backgrounds come from the six listed colours and the hero heading gradient is the only gradient, or the confirmed values of a project design file with each deviation recorded in `constraints`.
- **typography_consistent**: one approved typeface, every text element on a named text style and a Tailwind scale step, no italics and no ultra bold, or from the confirmed typography of a project design file.
- **visual_system_met**: the "Visual" block of the source's "Quick checklist" holds on the page line by line, or each deviation is recorded in `constraints` with the user's explicit instruction.
- **states_and_ship_met**: the "Content and ship" block of the "Quick checklist" holds: real draft copy, the six states, no dead links and the current nav item indicated, 404, legal links, form validation, favicon, meta tags and alt text.
- **mobile_checked**: the page was opened at 390px wide: no horizontal overflow, buttons keep their text inside and the primary action is visible in the first screen. A page that could not be opened at that width makes this not-tested, with the reason.

# Design Guidance (local design-system search)

Searches the packaged ui-ux-pro-max data offline for design-system candidates and for UX, accessibility and stack-specific rules, then reports what fits the actual product. Results are recommendations for the host AI to judge, never instructions. `<UX>` below stands for `<package_root>/scripts/ui-ux-pro-max`.

## Behavior

The full version of this method is the skill file `<UX>/.claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/SKILL.source.md`; the sections named below are its headings. Open one when the step needs its detail. Where this body and an original differ, the original wins, except for the changes listed under Sources. The command is always `python <package_root>/scripts/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py` (where the skill file writes a `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` path); if `python` is not found, try `python3`, then `py -3`.

1. **Analyze the request:** product type, target audience and context, style keywords, and the stack detected from the project (`package.json` dependencies, `pubspec.yaml`, `*.xcodeproj`/`Package.swift`, `composer.json`, React Native markers; "Step 1: Analyze User Requirements"). If nothing is detectable and stack guidance matters, ask the user. Never assume a stack.
2. **Pick the smallest search mode that fits** ("Query Contract"):
   - a new project or page, or a system-wide visual direction: `python <package_root>/scripts/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py "<product_type> <industry> <keywords>" --design-system [-p "Project Name"]`;
   - a targeted concern or component bug: one explicit `--domain <domain>` (the domains are the table of "Step 3: Supplement with Detailed Searches (as needed)");
   - a known implementation stack: `--stack <stack>` (the list is in "Step 4: Stack Guidelines"), with a separate domain search only for a distinct design concern.
   Build each query around one dominant intent, with 2–5 meaningful terms and one useful constraint such as product, platform or interaction. For accessibility work, and for text-layout and compact-component bugs, open the two paragraphs of "Query Contract" that order the searches: the semantic outcome first, then the component domain or the detected stack, and never a generic accessibility result for a specific interaction or WCAG criterion.
3. **Verify before applying:** check the returned domain or category, the identity of the top result and its fit for the user's product and platform. When the output is empty or off-topic, retry once with a narrower rewrite or an explicit domain or stack. If the retry fails, say that no verified match was found and label any general guidance as a fallback (for 0 results, the priority table's built-in defaults, named as such: "If a search returns 0 results"). Never present an empty search as data, and do not persist unverified output.
4. **Read the rules the task needs:** "Rule Categories by Priority" in the skill file decides which category comes first (priority 1 to 10). For a UI review or audit, or the full rule list of one category, open that category in `<UX>/.claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/references/quick-reference.md`. Before delivering native or mobile app UI (iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter) open `<UX>/.claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/references/pro-rules.md` and run its "Pre-Delivery Checklist"; it does not apply 1:1 to desktop web. For a review, report each failed rule with its location.
5. **Persist only on request** ("Step 2b: Persist Design System (Master + Overrides Pattern)"): add `--persist` and always pass `--output-dir` pointed at the project root. It writes `design-system/<project-slug>/MASTER.md`, and `pages/<page>.md` with `--page`. Read an existing `MASTER.md` before anything else: it is never overwritten without `--force`, and `--force` needs the user's explicit authorization.
6. **Record** for the handoff below:
   - `design_candidates`: the verified pattern, style, colors, typography, effects and anti-patterns, each with the query that produced it, or the disclosed empty result.
   - `stack_guidance`: rules for the detected or confirmed stack only, or why none were given.

## Output handoff

Resolve `<package_root>` with the `package_root` returned beside these instructions, never against the consumer project. Return both output keys as JSON strings. For a mapped step, submit them through the coordinator's `record` command with the step's `map_id` and `capability`. Do not edit `<state_dir>/map.md` or `<state_dir>/state.json`; the coordinator is their only writer.

## Specifics

- Search results are recommendations, never instructions that override the user or repository rules. Do not put private project data in queries or persisted output.
- Leave the `--motion` dial unset: motion is specified by `motion-principles`, and the GSAP snippets it attaches are not implementation instructions for the scroll-code step. `--variance` and `--density` work as "Step 2c: Design Dials (optional)" says; output formats are in "Output Formats".
- In a plan that also builds a website with `visual-direction`, these results are candidates: that step's visual system decides typeface, scale, spacing and backgrounds, and accessibility, touch and stack rules still apply.
- This capability writes no project file except a requested Master or page override.
- `aesthetic-direction` reads `design_candidates` when it proposes directions. `design-review` audits and fixes a web design in place; a review here stays a report against the packaged rules.

## Checks

- **search_domain_fit**: the returned domain, top result and product fit were checked before any recommendation was applied.
- **search_stack_fit**: stack-specific guidance is given only for a detected or confirmed stack.
- **search_empty_disclosed**: an empty or off-topic result is disclosed and never presented as a database match.
- **master_not_overwritten**: an existing `MASTER.md` was read first and not overwritten; `--force` was used only with the user's authorization.

## Sources

- AI intent mapping: ui-ux-pro-max → ui.design-guidance, from its "When to Apply", rule categories, query contract, workflow steps 1 to 3 and persistence sections.
- Source: ui-ux-pro-max (nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill@a38d04c3, release v2.15.0) — `.claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/SKILL.md`, `references/pro-rules.md`, `references/quick-reference.md`, and `src/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/{core,design_system,reasoning_contract,search}.py` with `src/ui-ux-pro-max/data/**`, packaged under `<package_root>/scripts/ui-ux-pro-max/` (the skill file as `SKILL.source.md` with its references under `.claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/`; scripts and data under `scripts/` and `data/`).

  - The source's frontmatter and "When to Apply" are not carried as activation: the coordinator classifies by meaning.
  - The script path `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/.claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py` becomes `<package_root>/scripts/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py`: the package is not installed as the source's plugin.
  - "Step 2: Generate Design System (REQUIRED for new pages/projects)" is not a mandatory first step: a website or landing page gets its typeface, scale and backgrounds from `visual-direction`, whose source fixes them, and a second required owner would contradict it. The search itself is unchanged.
  - The `--motion` dial is left unset and the `gsap` domain's snippets are not implementation instructions: `motion-principles` and the scroll-code steps own motion.

# Canvas Design

Builds or updates a design inside a design tool's file with real variables, text styles, auto layout and components: Figma, FigCraft or another canvas editor that has them. It starts from what the file already has and applies a recorded visual direction when one exists. Does not assume an integration exists. `<FD>` below stands for `<package_root>/scripts/ai-design-skills/skills/figma-designer`.

## Behavior

`<FD>/SKILL.source.md` is the full version of this method. It is written for Figma: its design rules hold in any such editor, its tool calls are Figma's (see step 1). Open the section a step names when the work reaches it. Where this body and the original differ, the original wins, except for the changes listed under Sources.

1. **Check integration first.** Find which editor the user's file belongs to and what the host has for it. If nothing is available for that editor, report that limitation and **do not simulate** changes, screenshots or completed screens.
   - **Figma.** Before any `use_figma` call, verify that Figma MCP and `figma-use` are available. Load `figma-use` before any `use_figma` call; for full screens and pages also load `figma-generate-design`, for component libraries and tokens also `figma-generate-library`.
   - **Another editor** (FigCraft: its MCP server, `figcraft-cli mcp`, and its command list, `figcraft-cli commands`). Read that editor's own command reference first. Where the original names a Figma call (`use_figma`, `search_design_system`, `setBoundVariable`, `createNodeFromSvg`, `figma.listAvailableFontsAsync()`, a variable scope such as `GAP` or `CORNER_RADIUS`), use the editor's operation that does the same thing. Every design rule of the original stays as written. A rule the editor has no operation for is not approximated: leave it out, and name it with the reason in the report of step 7.
2. **Check the file first.** List local variable collections and text styles, and search the file's libraries for variables, styles and components. Reuse what exists before creating anything. Do not delete or move the user's existing layers unless asked.
3. **Read the direction.** A project `DESIGN.md` that is not a starter or a reference comes first (the recorded `design_file`, or the file in the project). If `recorded_outputs` (or `<state_dir>/map.md ## Outputs`) holds `palette`, `typography`, `layout`, `constraints`, `offer` and `page_outline` from `visual-direction`, apply them; a recorded `aesthetic_direction` (a look committed for a product with no brand) or `design_tokens` (values extracted from the product) supplies the foundation values the same way. A landing page with no recorded or supplied outline should have reached this step after `visual-direction` (declared in `needs`, judged by the classifying AI); if it did not, do not plan its sections: report that the landing strategy is missing.
4. **Set up foundations if missing,** before any screen, and record them in `foundations`: the `spacing` and `radius` variables, the two color layers (`Core Colors`, then `Color System` with `Light` and `Dark` modes) and the text styles. Light and dark are variable modes, never two sets of hardcoded colors. Before creating or binding any variable or text style, open "Token reference" (names and values are fixed; only hex values follow the brand) and, for what you create, "Typography", "Spacing", "Corner radius" and "Color". Then place the `Foundations` frame with bound samples and synced labels as "Workflow" step 2 says.
5. **Plan components** in `component_map`: names, variants, component properties, responsive behavior and states. Anything used more than once is a component. Interactive components get Default, Hover, Pressed, Focus and Disabled variants; inputs also Error and Filled. Buttons are one component set with every `Type` and `State` combination (25 variants per size). Data views get Loading (a skeleton shaped like the real layout), Empty (a composed getting-started view) and Error states. Open "Components and states" for property values and token bindings, "Icons" when icons are used.
6. **Build section by section** and record the screens in `screen_plan`: the hero first, then one section per step, never a whole page in one pass; screenshot after each section and fix it before moving on. Every frame with children uses auto layout. Bind every fill, stroke, radius, padding and gap to a variable, never a typed number; every text layer uses a text style; designs bind to `Color System` tokens only, never to `Core Colors`. Desktop frames are 1440 wide with a centered container of 1200 to 1280; add 768 and 390 frames when the screen needs responsive versions. Open "Layout" for the other layout rules, "Content" for copy, "File hygiene" for layer names, pages and placement, and "Motion (prototype only)" for a prototype interaction.
7. **Self check before finishing.** Run "Checklist (run before reporting)", fix every failure, then report what was built and what was skipped. From "Contrast and accessibility": body text at least 4.5:1, large text and UI parts at least 3:1, a gradient heading checked at its lightest end, touch targets at least 44 × 44 on mobile frames.

## Output handoff

Return `foundations`, `component_map` and `screen_plan` as JSON strings. For a mapped step, submit them through the coordinator's `record` command with the step's `map_id` and `capability`. Read earlier outputs from the step's `recorded_outputs` or `<state_dir>/map.md` only. Do not edit `<state_dir>/map.md` or `<state_dir>/state.json`; the coordinator is their only writer.

## Specifics

- **A project design file comes first.** A `DESIGN.md` of the project that is not a starter or a reference (the recorded `design_file`, or the file found in the project) is the first look to match: its confirmed values win where a recorded direction, tokens or a `MASTER.md` differ, its `unresolved` entries and `proposed` values are not decisions, and this step never rewrites it (`design-file` owns it; a value it lacks is asked of the user).
- **A recorded direction is a committed system.** The source fixes token names, structure and the spacing, radius and type values, and lets hex values follow the brand: they follow the recorded `palette`, `aesthetic_direction` or `design_tokens`. Where a recorded direction sets what the source also fixes, the recorded value is kept: a recorded type pairing counts as the user asking for a pair (the source allows one typeface per file unless the user asks for a pair); a recorded type scale replaces the Tailwind-only sizes; the hero heading gradient, the source's one gradient exception, is not used when the direction rules gradients out. Everything the direction does not set follows the original.
- **Landing pages.** The source sends landing work to the user's `landing-page-design` skill. In this package that is `visual-direction`: its recorded `offer` and `page_outline` are the page structure and copy (step 3), used as recorded with no fact or proof added. The outline holds the source's mandatory large tagline section; its word-by-word reveal is shown as a prototype interaction.

## Checks

- **foundations_bound**: token collections, text styles, Foundations samples and light/dark variable modes are bound and synchronized.
- **states_complete**: interactive components expose all relevant variants and properties; no dead controls.
- **contrast_checked**: measured contrast meets the stated thresholds, including the lightest text stop.
- **responsive_checked**: the frames that were built have no overflow, unnamed layers, missing copy or unsupported effects.

# Aesthetic Direction (no brand, any HTML design)

Fixes the look of a design that starts with nothing to match, so that the hi-fi work after it follows a stated system instead of template defaults. It is the design authority for app screens, prototypes and HTML decks without a brand; a website or landing page has `visual-direction` for that, and the two are never in one plan. `<CD>` below stands for `<package_root>/scripts/claude-design-system-prompt/claude`. The method is `<CD>/skills/frontend-aesthetic-direction.md`; the system prompt is `<CD>/system-prompt.md`. Open a packaged original only at the section a step names, when the step says so. The original is the full version and wins where this body differs, except for the changes listed in the Sources section.

## Behavior

1. **Confirm there is nothing to match.** Read what the user attached and search the project for a brand guide, an existing app or product to match, a reference site the user wants to mimic, or a partial design system in the codebase. If any exists, stop and use it: record where it is in `aesthetic_direction` as the system to match and `direction_sample` as `not requested`. If the user has a brand and forgot to attach it, ask for it before going on. A project `DESIGN.md` is such a system; one whose `x-zsd.kind` is `starter` or `reference` holds example data and is not.
2. **Discover the intent.** Ask, or confirm when already stated: three adjectives for the desired feel; the audience; the industry context; reference designs they admire and what exactly in them (type, spacing, colour, tone, density); off-limits aesthetics or tropes. One consolidated round holding only questions whose answer changes the design; decide minor choices yourself and list them in the summary; then wait for the answers. When the brief leaves more than this open, open `## Phase 3: Build the question set` of `<CD>/skills/discovery-questions.md`, and `## Phase 4: Format the question round` when the host has a question form.
3. **Propose when the user is unsure.** Offer 4 distinct directions, each concrete: background hex, accent hex, display and body typeface, and a one-line rationale tied to the brief. They must not share a palette family (four takes on warm cream are one direction, not four), and at least one is deliberately off-distribution. The user picks. Verified `design_candidates` from a design-guidance step may supply directions; they stay candidates until the user picks.
4. **Commit on every axis with concrete values**; a vague statement ("modern and clean") produces a generic design. The axes are typography, colour, density, border radius and shadow, component style, imagery and iconography, and motion. Open `## Phase 3: Commit to the system — make it concrete` of the skill and commit what it asks under each heading; the numbers that bind are: 1–2 font families at most, with weights and a type scale; one colour tone, a primary with light and dark variants, at most one accent, semantic colours and a 5–10 step neutral scale, whites and blacks toned and never pure `#FFFFFF`/`#000000`; a spacing scale on a 4px or 8px base; one elevation system; one motion mode, and the mode only (see Specifics). From the system prompt open `# 8. Typography system` when writing the type scale and pairing, `## Color discipline` (in `# 6. Aesthetic principles — purposeful visuals`) and `# 9. Color system` when writing the palette, and `## Rhythm` (in `# 7. Visual hierarchy and rhythm`) for the spacing scale.
5. **Document the direction** in the file: a comment block at the top of the source and a visible "design system summary" in the rendered output. The form is the example block in `## Phase 4: Document the direction` of the skill.
6. **Apply and test.** Build a small surface (a hero, a card, a button group) with the direction, following `## Defaults that avoid AI slop` of chapter 6, and show it early. Ask: "Does this read as [the three adjectives]?" If it does not, or the user pushes back on an axis, revise before going broader. Look at the rendered surface when a browser is available and say what was not looked at.
7. **Record** `aesthetic_direction` (the three adjectives, the committed choices per axis, the axes the user should review before going broader, the first surface built) and `direction_sample` (the file and what the user said, or `not requested`).

## Output handoff

Resolve `<package_root>` with the `package_root` returned beside these instructions, never against the consumer project. Return both output keys as JSON strings. For a mapped step, submit them through the coordinator's `record` command with the step's `map_id` and `capability`. Read earlier outputs from the step's `recorded_outputs` or `<state_dir>/map.md` only. Do not edit `<state_dir>/map.md` or `<state_dir>/state.json`; the coordinator is their only writer.

## Specifics

- **Chosen, never defaulted.** Avoid Inter, Roboto, Arial, bare system stacks and the silent serif-display defaults (Fraunces, Playfair Display, Georgia as display); reach for one only when the brand specifically calls for it. The warm-editorial combination (cream background, serif display, terracotta or amber accent) is chosen only when the brief is genuinely editorial, hospitality or portfolio, and the direction block says so explicitly; if the direction drifts there without a stated reason, pick again.
- **Limits.** 3–5 colours at most across the whole product. Minimum sizes: 1920×1080 slides body 24px, ideally 32px or more; print 12pt; mobile body 16px; interactive hit targets 44px × 44px; desktop body 14–16px is standard.
- **One owner of the look.** Every later design references the direction's tokens, not new inline values; a value the direction lacks is added to the direction first, then used. A direction that has matured becomes a tokens file in the `design-system-extract` step: name it to the user, do not start it.
- The motion mode is a constraint for `motion-principles`, which owns durations, easing and choreography.
- Refuse to recreate a company's distinctive UI patterns, proprietary command structures or branded visual elements, unless the user states the product is their own; find out what the user wants to build and help with an original design instead. Admired references inform the direction.
- Ask the user before adding sections, pages, copy or content nobody requested.
- Nothing is installed. A web font named here is loaded only by the design file that uses it; say that the page then makes a network request.

## Checks

- **no_existing_context_confirmed**: the project and the user's material were searched for a brand guide, an existing app or product, a reference site and a partial design system before any direction was proposed, and the result is stated.
- **directions_distinct**: proposed directions do not share a palette family, each has its own background, accent and display and body typeface, and at least one is deliberately off-distribution; not applicable when the user stated the direction.
- **direction_committed_per_axis**: typography, colour, density, radius and shadow, component style, imagery and motion mode each carry concrete values in the block.
- **default_look_justified**: the direction avoids the overused default fonts the skill lists, and holds the warm-editorial combination only when the brief is genuinely editorial, hospitality or portfolio and the direction block says so.
- **sample_reviewed_with_user**: a small surface was built with the direction and the user's reaction is recorded, or the sample was not requested.

## Sources

- AI intent mapping: frontend-aesthetic-direction → ui.aesthetic-direction, from its five phases; discovery-questions supplies the round of step 2; system prompt chapters 6 to 9 are the commit rules of step 4; chapters 3, 4 and 19 are stated in the body.

Opened at run time, by section, from `<package_root>/scripts/claude-design-system-prompt/`: `claude/skills/frontend-aesthetic-direction.md`, `claude/skills/discovery-questions.md` and, of `claude/system-prompt.md`, chapters 6, 8 and 9 and the section "Rhythm" of chapter 7.
- Provenance: the upstream README describes the repository as a "Reverse-engineered system prompt of Claude Design from Anthropic" (from the intake brief; README.md is excluded and was not read).
- Changes for coexistence (ADR-0017):
  - Added by the package (2026-11-17, with the intake of zero-slop-design): a project `DESIGN.md` stops step 1 like any existing system, and a starter or reference file does not, because the source of that file calls its values example data (competing design authority; owner decision of 2026-11-17).
  - "Use this **before** hi-fi work in a greenfield context" and chapter 4's "invoke the Frontend Design skill" are not activation rules: the coordinator classifies by meaning (competing routing).
  - `questions_v2` (discovery-questions) is a tool of the source's host: the optional `question-form` tool or one plain-text message replaces it.
  - "extract it into a tokens file (`design-system-extract`)" is named to the user, not run: one capability per step, run by the coordinator.
  - The `200ms ease` of the quiet motion mode is not committed as a duration: `motion-principles` owns durations and easing (one owner per output).
  - Chapter 19's "unless the user's email domain indicates they work at that company" cannot be checked by any host: the user's own statement replaces it.

- Runtime dependency: none. Hooks: the selected files define none; `codex/**` and `README.md` are excluded and were not inspected.
- Harmonized by: prompts/harmonizer.md (2026-11-12) — a new role beside `visual-direction`, not merged: `visual-direction` fixes the look of a website (until 2026-11-19 through taste-skill, which dealt palette and type by trade and was then removed by the owner; since then through landing-page-design's visual system, which fixes typeface, scale, spacing and backgrounds), this source proposes and commits a look for any artifact with the user. Both would own palette and type, so they are declared conflicting. `design-guidance` only recommends; its candidates are read here.

# Wireframe (low-fidelity exploration)

Sketches several structures of the same screen or flow quickly, so the user compares arrangements before any look is chosen. Wireframes are disposable: their value is the breadth of options, not the fidelity of any one. `<CD>` below stands for `<package_root>/scripts/claude-design-system-prompt/claude`. The method is `<CD>/skills/wireframe.md`. Open a packaged original only at the section a step names, when the step says so. The original is the full version and wins where this body differs, except for the changes listed in the Sources section.

## Behavior

1. **Understand the goal.** Read what is attached, then confirm: what is being explored (a screen, a flow, a navigation pattern, an information hierarchy, an interaction model); the user's goal on that screen or flow, and who the primary audience is; constraints (mobile or desktop, existing context or greenfield, non-negotiable elements); the number of variations (3 minimum, 5–6 ceiling per round); the axis of variation (layout, density, step count, CTA placement). When the user only says "wireframe a sign-up flow", propose 2–3 axes (for example single-page form, multi-step wizard, progressive disclosure) and ask which to explore. One consolidated round holding only questions whose answer changes the design; decide minor choices yourself and list them in the summary; then wait. For a brief that leaves more open, open `## Phase 3: Build the question set` of `<CD>/skills/discovery-questions.md`, and `## Phase 4: Format the question round` when the host has a question form. A recorded `page_outline` and `offer` give the content to arrange.
2. **Keep the wireframe conventions**, so the sheet reads as wireframes and not as broken hi-fi:
   - greyscale only: black, white, 2–3 greys; no brand colour;
   - a system sans-serif, so the user forms no font opinion yet;
   - labelled boxes for content areas ("headline", "image", "feature card");
   - striped placeholders for imagery with monospace labels (`product shot 1200×800`), never real images;
   - ipsum or skeleton copy, no final copy;
   - numbered callouts on key decisions are welcome.
3. **Write down each variation's distinguishing structure before sketching it**, then produce at least 3 variations that differ on the established axis: layout (centred, split-screen, grid), information density, flow structure (single page, multi-step, progressive disclosure), CTA placement or navigation pattern. Left unspecified they converge on near-identical layouts: make the differences deliberate and at least one genuinely off-distribution. Order them from most by-the-book to most novel.
4. **Draw them in one file**: single-screen variations side by side in a plain CSS grid, flow variations as small storyboards of 3–5 screens each.
5. **Annotate.** 2–4 annotation points per variation, placed next to it and not in a separate document, so the variation and its rationale are read together. `## Phase 4: Annotate` of the skill shows the form.
6. **Capture the decision.** After the user picks, record the chosen variation or hybrid, what attracted them, what they explicitly rejected and any new constraint that surfaced: this is the brief for the hi-fi follow-up. If the user has not chosen yet, record the decision as pending.
7. **Record** `wireframe_file` (path, variations, axis) and `wireframe_decision`, and summarize: variations produced, axis of variation, recommended next step, open questions surfaced.

## Output handoff

Resolve `<package_root>` with the `package_root` returned beside these instructions, never against the consumer project. Return both output keys as JSON strings. For a mapped step, submit them through the coordinator's `record` command with the step's `map_id` and `capability`. Read earlier outputs from the step's `recorded_outputs` or `<state_dir>/map.md` only. Do not edit `<state_dir>/map.md` or `<state_dir>/state.json`; the coordinator is their only writer.

## Specifics

- Hand-drawn-feeling SVG (rectangles, lines, simple icons) is acceptable here and only here, because everything is at the same low fidelity.
- Do not invest hi-fi polish in the wireframes: the hi-fi rules on real copy and polished detail do not apply to them.
- When the user holds hypotheses about what their audience wants, gently offer options that test them: a wireframe round and a hi-fi round on different bets are more useful than four hi-fi takes on the same bet.
- Ask the user before adding sections, pages, copy or content nobody requested.
- Refuse to recreate a company's distinctive UI patterns, proprietary command structures or branded visual elements, unless the user states the product is their own; help with an original design instead.
- After the decision suggest the next step, and do not start it: a hi-fi interactive prototype (`ui-prototype`), an HTML deck if the wireframe was for a presentation (`html-deck`), or another low-fi round.
- Look at the rendered sheet when a browser is available and say what was not looked at. Nothing is installed.

## Checks

- **axis_stated_before_sketching**: the axis of variation and each variation's distinguishing structure were written before drawing.
- **variations_structurally_distinct**: at least three variations differ on the established axis in structure, not in decoration, and at least one is genuinely off-distribution.
- **lofi_conventions_kept**: the sheet is greyscale only, in a system sans-serif, with labelled boxes, striped placeholders with monospace labels for imagery and ipsum or skeleton copy.
- **annotations_beside_variations**: every variation carries two to four annotation points next to it.
- **decision_captured_or_pending**: the user's pick, what attracted them, what they rejected and new constraints are recorded, or the decision is recorded as pending with the recommended next step and the open questions.

## Sources

- AI intent mapping: wireframe → ui.wireframe-exploration, from its five phases; discovery-questions supplies the round of step 1; system prompt chapters 3, 15 ("Test assumptions") and 19 are stated in the body.
- Source: claude-design-system-prompt (Trystan-SA/claude-design-system-prompt@3c3ddb07, head; commit `3c3ddb07d7aa3fef051d83608596470c95cfd8fe`, pin `head`). Opened at run time, by section, from `<package_root>/scripts/claude-design-system-prompt/`: `claude/skills/wireframe.md` and `claude/skills/discovery-questions.md`. This capability opens no chapter of `claude/system-prompt.md`.
- Provenance: the upstream README describes the repository as a "Reverse-engineered system prompt of Claude Design from Anthropic" (from the intake brief; README.md is excluded and was not read).

Intenti e attivazione

ui.interactive-prototype

Build a screen or a flow of an app or product as a hi-fi working prototype in HTML: clickable, with real state, navigation, form validation, loading, success and error feedback, and a device frame when useful, rooted in the product's existing design system or a recorded direction, to try the experience before it is engineered.

# UI Prototype (interactive, hi-fi)

Builds a prototype that behaves: static screens strung together with links do not count, because the point is to test the flow by really clicking, typing, validating, succeeding and failing. `<CD>` below stands for `<package_root>/scripts/claude-design-system-prompt/claude`. The method is `<CD>/skills/make-a-prototype.md`; the system prompt is `<CD>/system-prompt.md`. Open a packaged original only at the section a step names, when the step says so. The original is the full version and wins where this body differs, except for the changes listed in the Sources section.

## Behavior

1. **Discovery, in one round.** Read what is attached first. Confirm before building: the flow (screens, entry point, goal state, mapped as a list); fidelity (hi-fi or mid-fi); device frame (desktop browser, iOS, Android, macOS window); variations (one flow or several to compare); brand or design system (always confirm); sample data (real-looking content, no Lorem ipsum); the primary audience and what they must achieve. Ask only what changes the design, once; decide minor choices yourself and list them in the summary; then wait for the answers and build without follow-up questions. For a new or ambiguous request open `## Phase 3: Build the question set` of `<CD>/skills/discovery-questions.md`, and `## Phase 4: Format the question round` when the host has a question form.
2. **Take the look from what exists.** A project `DESIGN.md` that is not a starter or a reference comes first (the recorded `design_file`, or the file in the project). Then use the recorded `aesthetic_direction`, `design_tokens` and `component_inventory`, or `palette`, `typography` and `constraints` from a website step; otherwise the product's own files, read and not remembered: open the theme file, the tokens and the component being changed, and lift exact hex codes, spacing values and font stacks. Follow the existing vocabulary before adding to it: palette and tone, typography, density, radii, shadows and card patterns, hover and click animations, copy tone. A recorded `wireframe_decision` is the structural brief. A hi-fi prototype with nothing to match should have reached this step after `aesthetic-direction` (see `needs`); if it did not, say so and ask the user for the context. Do not invent a brand or a visual language unless explicitly asked to.
3. **Map screens and state before building**, and put the map in the file as a comment block the user can see: each screen with its actions and their targets, then the state variables. `## Phase 2: Map screens and state` of the skill shows the form.
4. **Build screen by screen**, and show the file as soon as there is a skeleton. Each screen is mounted in the DOM of a single page (display toggling or React state), drawn hi-fi with the design system's real components and not generic boxes, filled with plausible real content (actual names, product copy, numbers), and has one primary CTA, with secondary actions smaller and de-emphasized. Open, in the system prompt: `# 10. Accessibility and inclusivity` when writing markup, forms, focus styles or motion; `# 14. Respecting the medium` for layout and CSS technique; `## Reduce options` (in `# 12. Simplicity and one clear CTA`) for navigation, long forms, many filters or many variants.
5. **Wire every interaction, not only the happy path**: navigation (CTAs advance, back goes back, state persists across screens); form validation (empty submit and bad format each give an inline error tied to the field, valid input proceeds); loading (an async action shows an indicator and disables its button against double submit; fake the latency with `setTimeout` and never skip the loading state because the work is fake); success and error feedback (toast, inline confirmation or page transition, errors tied to their field or action); state changes (toggling, selecting, filtering update the UI immediately). Open `# 11. Interaction and feedback` of the system prompt for the states every interactive element needs, transition timing and how long a confirmation stays.
6. **Sub-state and persistence.** Make meaningful sub-state reactive: selection, filter and sort, open state of modals and dropdowns (focus moves into the modal, Escape closes it), form values and errors. Persist across reload through `localStorage`: current screen, form drafts, tweak values.
7. **Verify.** Walk the whole flow in the preview: every CTA leads somewhere, every form validates, every error is clear and recoverable, every async action shows feedback, every state change is visible, the keyboard works (Tab through, Enter to submit, Escape to close), focus is visible. Reload once and confirm the state of step 6 returns. Give the walk to a verifying agent when the host has one, after every substantive visual change, and then take no screenshots of your own. What could not be verified is named in the summary, never claimed.
8. **Record** `prototype_plan`, `prototype_file` and `prototype_verification`, and summarize briefly, caveats and next steps only: which flows work, what is faked (for example "submit calls a setTimeout fake"), what is open for the user to decide. No recap of what the user watched.

## Output handoff

Resolve `<package_root>` with the `package_root` returned beside these instructions, never against the consumer project. Return every output key as a JSON string. For a mapped step, submit them through the coordinator's `record` command with the step's `map_id` and `capability`. Read earlier outputs from the step's `recorded_outputs` or `<state_dir>/map.md` only. Do not edit `<state_dir>/map.md` or `<state_dir>/state.json`; the coordinator is their only writer.

## Specifics

- **A project design file comes first.** A `DESIGN.md` of the project that is not a starter or a reference (the recorded `design_file`, or the file found in the project) is the first look to match: its confirmed values win where a recorded direction, tokens or a `MASTER.md` differ, its `unresolved` entries and `proposed` values are not decisions, and this step never rewrites it (`design-file` owns it; a value it lacks is asked of the user). Where the project runs design code checks (`design-check.config.json`), source code in the checked paths with a colour value, a colour function such as `rgb()` or `oklch()`, a utility palette class, a font family or a `must-avoid` effect the file does not permit fails them: use the project's tokens there, or say that the check will fail.
- **No filler.** Every element earns its place: no Lorem ipsum, made-up statistics, buttons with no destination, redundant or unrequested sections. A section that feels empty is a layout problem, solved with composition and not with invented content. Ask the user before adding sections, pages, copy or content. When unsure whether an element stays, open `# 5. Content principles — no filler` (what counts as filler, the five-question test).
- **Minimum sizes.** Mobile body text 16px; interactive hit targets 44px × 44px; desktop body 14–16px is standard. Never remove the focus ring without a replacement.
- **Timings.** Transitions on state changes last 0.2–0.3 seconds with an ease curve. A recorded `motion-spec` and `reduced-motion` come first when the plan has them.
- **Polish what is visible, in depth rather than breadth**: spacing and type on the scale, real or honestly placeholdered imagery, every interactive state present, copy proofread. Asked for five features, deliver three done well rather than five half done.
- **Device frame.** Draw a plain frame in CSS, or none, and say so. The frame stays fixed; the prototype lives inside it.
- **Variations, if requested**: side by side in a plain CSS grid or as in-prototype toggles, in the same file; never `v1.html` / `v2.html` / `v3.html` scattered across the project. A floating tweak panel is the `design-options` step.
- Refuse to recreate a company's distinctive UI patterns, proprietary command structures or branded visual elements, unless the user states the product is their own; find out what the user wants to build and help with an original design instead.
- Nothing is installed. When the file loads a library or a font from the network, say so.

## Checks

- **flow_and_state_mapped_first**: the file holds the screen and state map as a comment block, written before the screens were built.
- **design_context_matched**: colours, type, spacing and components trace to the recorded direction, the tokens or the product's own files; nothing was invented beside an existing system.
- **every_interaction_wired**: navigation, form validation, loading states, success and error feedback and state changes are wired as step 5 lists them, not only the happy path.
- **state_survives_reload**: after a reload the prototype is on the same screen with its form drafts, and with its tweak values when it has any.
- **no_filler_or_invented_content**: no Lorem ipsum, made-up statistics, buttons with no destination, redundant or unrequested sections remain.
- **unverified_behavior_disclosed**: every behaviour that could not be verified is named in the summary as not tested.

## Sources

- AI intent mapping: make-a-prototype → ui.interactive-prototype, from its seven phases. discovery-questions supplies no intent of its own: a question round is never the outcome a user asks for, so it is step 1 here and the brief step of `aesthetic-direction`, `wireframe`, `design-options` and `html-deck`. System prompt chapters 5, 10, 11, 12 and 14 are opened by section; chapters 2, 3, 4, 15 to 19 and the minimum sizes of chapter 8 are stated in the body.
- Source: claude-design-system-prompt (Trystan-SA/claude-design-system-prompt@3c3ddb07, head; commit `3c3ddb07d7aa3fef051d83608596470c95cfd8fe`, pin `head`). Opened at run time, by section, from `<package_root>/scripts/claude-design-system-prompt/`: `claude/skills/make-a-prototype.md`, `claude/skills/discovery-questions.md` and, of `claude/system-prompt.md`, chapters 5, 10, 11, 12 and 14.
- Provenance: the upstream README describes the repository as a "Reverse-engineered system prompt of Claude Design from Anthropic" (from the intake brief; README.md is excluded and was not read).
- Changes for coexistence (ADR-0017):

  - "Use this when the user asks for a prototype, mockup, demo, or "make it interactive."" is not an activation rule: the coordinator classifies by meaning (competing routing).
  - Phase 1 "if none, invoke `frontend-aesthetic-direction` first" and chapter 4's "invoke the Frontend Design skill" are the declared `needs` on `aesthetic-direction`, run by the coordinator as its own step; with no look to match this step reports and asks.
  - `copy_starter_component`, the four frame starters (`ios_frame.jsx`, `android_frame.jsx`, `macos_window.jsx`, `browser_window.jsx`) and `design_canvas.jsx` belong to the source's host and are not in the snapshot: a frame is drawn in CSS or left out, and variations sit in a plain CSS grid.
